notes.lines: Every precinct line is the Secretary of State's, generalised by at most 1.5 metres and set on a grid of 0.00001 degree (about a metre). A point within a few metres of a line can fall on either side of it.
notes.precincts: A shape is a precinct as the county auditor drew it for the August 4, 2026 primary, the newest statewide file the Secretary of State has published. The county elections office is the authority on which precinct an address is in.
notes.districts: Each precinct's congressional and legislative district is the Secretary of State's own table. Washington elects both members of the House and its senator from one legislative district, so house and senate are the same number.
notes.places: Washington's cities and towns, by the Census Bureau's 2025 lines. A precinct's mcd is the place holding half or more of it (absent outside every city and town); mcd_all lists every place it reaches where it reaches more than one or lies partly outside: to say which place a point is in, ask the mcd layer, not the precinct.
notes.commissioners: Council and commissioner districts are drawn for Clark County, King County, Pierce County, Spokane County, each from the county's own lines (Pierce from the Auditor's precinct table). Most counties nominate commissioners by district in the primary and elect them countywide in November, so their races are placed on the whole county. Yakima and Franklin elect by district and their lines are not drawn here.
notes.judicial: Where a county's district court is elected by electoral district, the districts are drawn for Clallam County, King County, Kittitas County, Pierce County, Snohomish County from the counties' own lines; eight Pierce County precincts vote in King County District Court's Southeast Electoral District. Elsewhere the district court is elected countywide and its races are placed on the county. Klickitat's and Pacific's two district courts each are not drawn. Court of Appeals districts are whole counties (RCW 2.06.020); coa names a precinct's.
notes.wards: Seattle's seven council districts are drawn from King County's file. No other city's council districts are drawn.
notes.school: School district lines are the Census Bureau's 2025 file. Which districts a precinct lies in is analysis, not an official list: a district counts when its part of the precinct is at least 60 metres thick somewhere; school_pct is each district's share of the precinct (land and water, not voters).
notes.polling: Washington votes by mail: there are no polling places. The map's sites are the ballot drop boxes and voting centers on the Secretary of State's statewide list.
notes.authority: For which precinct and districts an address is in, and where to return a ballot, the county elections office and VoteWA are the authority.
notes.precinct_ids: A precinct's id is the Secretary of State's code for it: two letters for the county and the precinct's number in eight digits (KI00002338 is King County precinct 2338).
